### Observed differences

- Three activities that were absent or nearly absent in the earlier window occur regularly in the later window: A19 in about 38 in 100 traces, A25 in about 35 in 100, and A20 in about 30 in 100; before, A19 and A25 were never observed and A20 appeared in only 1 of 200 traces. When they occur, they sit at roughly one-third of the trace's length (median relative position about 0.35). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, POS001, POS003]
- Routing after A41 changed: before, about 82 in 100 of A41's observed outgoing transitions went to A26; in the later window they go mainly to the new activities (A19 about 33 in 100, A25 about 30 in 100, A20 about 24 in 100), while transitions to A26 drop to about 1–2 in 100. [DIR004]
- The new activities in turn feed into A26: about 95 in 100 of A19's and 90 in 100 of A25's observed outgoing transitions lead to A26. [DIR002, DIR003]
- Consequently, the distance from A41 to A26 grew: before, A26 followed A41 within one step in about 82 in 100 cases; in the later window a two-step gap is typical (about 83 in 100), with about 14 in 100 spanning three steps. A26 still occurs in every trace in both windows, at a slightly later relative position (median about 0.36 to about 0.39). [LAG001, POS004]
- A02's observed outgoing transitions were also redistributed: A26 was its most common successor before (about 26 in 100) and is not observed after, while A16 rises to about 18 in 100 and many small new edges appear; this rests on only 35 vs 44 observed transitions. [DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, a new step is inserted between A41 and A26: after A41, the flow typically passes through one of the newly appearing activities A19, A25 or A20 — roughly one of the three per trace — before reaching A26, whereas before, A41 led directly to A26 in about 82 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions. The relational evidence shows this directly and consistently: A41's transitions moved from A26 to the three new activities, the new activities lead back to A26 in about 90–95 in 100 of their transitions, and the A41→A26 distance shifted from one step to mostly two steps while A26 remained present in every trace. The twelve qualifying items also far exceed the fewer than one expected by chance among the 95 tested control-flow units, so the pattern as a whole is not what an unchanged process typically produces. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR004, DIR002, DIR003, LAG001, POS004]

Limitations: no outgoing-transition profile is reported for A20, so its role in the inserted step rests only on A41's transitions and its occurrence pattern; and the evidence cannot establish that exactly one of the three activities is inserted in every trace, since about 14 in 100 of the A41→A26 distances span three steps. An important competing explanation that cannot be ruled out is that the three activities also occur elsewhere in traces, or that other routing around A41 changed at the same time; the direct transition and lag evidence makes a pure sampling artefact unlikely but does not exclude these alternatives. [LAG001, DIR004]

Other differences: A02's observed outgoing transitions shifted away from A26 (about 26 in 100 before, unobserved after) toward A16 (about 18 in 100 after), with many small new edges appearing; with only 35 and 44 observed transitions behind the two profiles, this may be sampling variation or a separate change, and A02 is not part of the main hypothesis. [DIR001]
